newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANI sells German water unit for A$104 mln.
newsitem.headline: ANI sells German water unit for A$104 mln.

text.p: Australian National Industries Ltd (ANI) said on Thursday it had settled the sale of its German waste water treatment business SHW Holter Wassertechnik GmbH to German ultility Berliner Wasser for a total of A$104.5 million.
ANI said it has also agreed with SHW, subject to pre-emptive rights held by building materials group Faxe Falk A/S, to buy ANI's 50 percent interest in BioBalance A/S for A$7.5 million.
BioBalance is a Danish company which has developed enhanced technology for the cost-effective management of operating systems used in waste water treatement.

"An abnormal gain of approximately A$13.0 million is expected to be realised on the sale of SHW and BioBalance," ANI said. However, this gain was likley to be offset by abnormal losses from restructuring costs and provisions for ANI's proposed sale of Holter businesses, it said.

ANI said the sale of SHW would not effect its ongoing commitment to its Australian waste joint venture, ANI-Kruger Pty Ltd. It said it had also decided to close the Holter group's engineering activity, Holter Industrie Technik.
It said Holter Industrie Technik would be closed following the completion of its existing obligations which were expected to be fufilled by December 1997.
ANI managing director Peter Stancliffe said in a statement that the sale of SHW and BioBalance virtually halved ANI's asset exposure to environmental engineering in Europe.

"However, although we are continuing to make progress with completion of Holter waster-to-energy contracts, we still have a number of open issues to manage in relation to Holter activities," Stancliffe said.
"We are continuing to give maximum priority to completion of projects as well as the restructuring of our involvement," he said.
At 11.15 a.m. (0115 GMT), ANI shares were one cent up at A$1.47.
